Approximately 30% of children with early-onset oppositional defant disorder go on to develop conduct disorder. The other choices are relatively protective and account for positive support.

questions.question_text: What is the lifetime prevalence of bipolar I disorder?
questions.explanation: Data from the National Comorbidity Survey Replication found a lifetime prevalence of bipolar I disorder of 1%. The lifetime prevalence of bipolar II was 1.1%, and the lifetime prevalence for any bipolar-related disorder was 4.4%.

questions.question_text: A 5-year-old boy is brought to the clinic by his parents with complaints of bedwetting for the past 3 months. The boy's bedwetting episodes occur about 3 times per week, and his parents are concerned about whether these symptoms will persist into adulthood. What is the best answer to their question?

options.text: Most patients with bedwetting will experience remission of symptoms as they age.
Once diagnosed, most patients with bedwetting will continue to have symptoms of similar severity into adulthood.
Symptoms will improve only if the patient is treated with pharmacological interventions.
Symptoms will initially improve and then worsen with age.

correct_answer.text: Most patients with bedwetting will experience remission of symptoms as they age.

correct_answers.text: Most patients with bedwetting will experience remission of symptoms as they age.

questions.explanation: Enuresis is the repeated voiding of urine in inappropriate situations such as on the bed or clothing. A developmental age of at least 5 is required to make the diagnosis. The prevalence is thought to be 5% to 10% in 5-year-olds, and this number decreases with age. The yearly spontaneous remission rate has been reported to be anywhere from 5% to 16%, with only 1% of patients retaining a diagnosis of enuresis into adulthood. Use of a bed alarm (i.e., behavioral management) is first-line treatment.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the official position of the American Psychiatric Association regarding therapeutic techniques aimed at changing a homosexual orientation?

options.text: They are indicated for select patients.
They deserve greater attention in ongoing research.
They are indicated as long as the therapist has appropriate training.
They should be offered to patients undergoing gender reassignment surgery.
They should be opposed for assuming that homosexual orientation should be changed.

correct_answer.text: They should be opposed for assuming that homosexual orientation should be changed.

correct_answers.text: They should be opposed for assuming that homosexual orientation should be changed.

questions.explanation: Since DSM-II, the American Psychiatric Association (APA) has eliminated the diagnosis of homosexuality as a mental disorder, and since that time gender identity and sexual orientation have been areas of increasing attention by the APA. The current position states, “The American Psychiatric Association opposes any psychiatric treatment, such as ‘reparative’ or ‘conversion’ therapy, which is based upon the assumption that homosexuality per se is a mental disorder, or based upon a prior assumption that the patient should change his/her homosexual orientation.”

questions.question_text: A 9-year-old boy with a family history of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and substance use disorder is brought to the clinic by his mother for evaluation of inattention, hyperactivity, and poor academic performance. After making a diagnosis of ADHD in the patient, you recommend treatment with a stimulant. The mother is concerned about the family history of substance use and asks you how treatment with a stimulant will impact the risk of developing a substance use disorder in the patient. Which of the following is the best response?

options.text: It is likely to increase the likelihood of developing a substance use disorder.
It is likely to decrease the likelihood of developing a substance use disorder.
It should have no impact on the likelihood of developing a substance use disorder.
It will increase the likelihood of developing only cocaine use disorder.

correct_answer.text: It is likely to decrease the likelihood of developing a substance use disorder.

correct_answers.text: It is likely to decrease the likelihood of developing a substance use disorder.

questions.explanation: A diagnosis of ADHD is itself a risk factor for the development of substance use; however, treatment for ADHD with a stimulant is considered to decrease the future likelihood of developing a substance use disorder.
